description: Dragon and Dog compatibility in the Chinese zodiac: Liu Chong (six clashes), their Earth and Earth elements, yin-yang, and what helps the pairing.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Dragon and the Dog are a Liu Chong (six clashes) pairing, with Earth and Earth as fixed elements (both earth). The Dragon brings vitality, ambition and confidence and the Dog loyalty, fairness and protectiveness. The tradition reads these as themes to work with, not a verdict.

sections.heading: How the Dragon and the Dog relate
paragraphs: With the Dog, the Dragon tends to bring vitality, generosity and big plans to a relationship. It often makes a partner feel part of something exciting. With the Dragon, the Dog tends to bring loyalty, honesty and protective care to a relationship. It often becomes a partner's most reliable ally. What the Dragon tends to value most in a partner is admiration balanced with honesty, and the strength to stand beside it as an equal. Grand gestures, bold dreams and an appreciative audience tend to keep a Dragon's heart engaged. Magnificent ambitions shared openly rarely fail to captivate it. What the Dog tends to value most in a partner is loyalty, fairness and consistency between words and actions. Steadfast reliability, fair play and heartfelt reassurance usually secure a Dog's devotion.

On first meeting, the Dragon often comes across as confident, lively and impressive. Meeting for the first time, the Dog often comes across as sincere, friendly and a little cautious. Traditional readings associate the Dragon with vitality, ambition and confidence and the Dog with loyalty, fairness and protectiveness. On the twelve-animal wheel the Dragon and the Dog sit six branches apart, directly opposite each other. Opposite animals form the Liu Chong clashes, and the Dragon and the Dog are traditionally described as strongly contrasting, sometimes magnetic, sometimes combative.

sections.heading: The traditional link: Liu Chong (six clashes)
paragraphs: The Dragon and the Dog are a Liu Chong pair, one of the six clashes. Both have Earth as their fixed element and sit opposite each other on the wheel. Traditional readings contrast the Dragon's grand ambitions with the Dog's practical principles, a pairing in which idealism and realism can either check each other usefully or lock into argument.

Liu Chong, the six clashes, pairs each animal with the one directly opposite it on the wheel. Traditional readings treat these as the most challenging pairings, describing tension rather than impossibility, and many such couples are said to learn a great deal from each other. Each animal has exactly one Liu Chong partner, so for the Dragon that partner is the Dog, and for the Dog it is the Dragon. The Dragon belongs to the Water trine with the Rat and Monkey, and the Dog to the Fire trine with the Tiger and Horse. In the traditional double-hour clock, the Dragon names the hours from 7 am to 9 am and the Dog those from 7 pm to 9 pm.

sections.heading: Five elements and yin-yang
paragraphs: The Dragon and the Dog share Earth as their fixed element. In five-element thinking that shared Earth is read as mutual recognition between the Dragon and the Dog, with the caution that the Dragon's and the Dog's excesses can double up as easily as their strengths. The Dragon and the Dog are both Yang animals, so the Dragon and the Dog share a more outward, active polarity. In five-element terms Earth is associated with stability and nourishment, a quality the Dragon and the Dog hold in common.

In everyday terms, the shared Earth of the Dragon and the Dog suggests stability, patience and practical care, with the caution that a steady Dragon and a steady Dog can become set in their ways. Each birth year also carries its own element from the heavenly stems, so a Metal Dragon differs from a Water Dragon, and a Wood Dog from a Fire Dog; a full reading compares those year elements too. For example, the most recent Dragon year, 2024, was a Wood year, and the most recent Dog year, 2018, an Earth year.

sections.heading: Needs, friction and what helps
paragraphs: With the Dog, the Dragon usually needs admiration, honesty and a partner with their own strength and ambitions. With the Dragon, the Dog usually needs trust, sincerity and reassurance, along with a partner who shares its values.

Under stress with the Dog, the Dragon can become proud, domineering or impatient, and may find it hard to admit it was wrong. Under stress with the Dragon, the Dog can become anxious, pessimistic or defensive, and may hold firmly to a principle when flexibility would help.

What helps the Dog with a Dragon is honest feedback delivered with respect, shared ambitions and genuine appreciation for its efforts. What helps the Dragon with a Dog is consistency, open explanations of decisions and reassurance during uncertain periods.

After an argument, the Dragon may find it hard to admit fault, and a Dog who acknowledges its good intentions first makes reconciliation easier. For its part, after an argument, the Dog usually needs to know the relationship is secure, and a Dragon who reassures it directly helps the Dog let go.

sections.heading: The Dragon and the Dog day to day
paragraphs: At home, the Dragon tends to think big, planning renovations, celebrations and ambitious projects, and appreciating a Dog who shares its enthusiasm. Celebrations in a Dragon household tend to be generous, memorable and slightly theatrical. At home, the Dog tends to be protective and dependable, appreciating a Dragon who is honest and consistent. Neighbours, friends and family are usually welcome in a Dog household, and looked after well.

As a colleague, the Dragon inspires and drives ambitious goals; beside the Dog, it brings vision and the confidence to pursue it. Pitches, transformations and ambitious launches are where the Dragon's energy is often most useful. As a colleague, the Dog upholds fairness and stays loyal under pressure; beside the Dragon, it offers steadiness and integrity. Compliance, advocacy and team leadership in difficult times are where the Dog often stands out. Shared projects that draw on the Dragon's vitality and the Dog's loyalty tend to show this pairing at its best.

faq.question: Are the Dragon and the Dog compatible in the Chinese zodiac?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Dragon and the Dog are a Liu Chong (six clashes) pairing. That describes a tendency, not a verdict; for the Dragon and the Dog, the themes to watch are the Dragon's pride and the Dog's worry.

faq.question: What are the elements of the Dragon and the Dog?
faq.answer: The Dragon's fixed element is Earth (Yang) and the Dog's is Earth (Yang); in the five-element cycles, both earth. Each birth year adds a separate year element.

faq.question: Which San He trine do the Dragon and the Dog belong to?
faq.answer: The Dragon belongs to the Water trine and the Dog to the Fire trine, so they are not trine mates.

faq.question: What might the Dragon and the Dog enjoy doing together?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Dragon usually enjoys grand, exciting outings such as festivals, luxury trips, performances and ambitious shared projects, while the Dog usually enjoys wholesome, loyal pastimes such as walks with friends, volunteering, outdoor activities and family gatherings. Alternating who chooses gives both a taste of the other's world.

faq.question: Does the Chinese zodiac use the calendar year?
faq.answer: No. Animal years begin at Lunar New Year: the Dragon year of 2024 began on February 10 and the Dog year of 2018 on February 16, so January birthdays need checking. The calculator does this automatically.
